rationale: The mac window host emitted its three GPU spans (gpu_acquire, gpu_submit, gpu_present) under the render category while the offscreen Skia path emitted the same three names under gpu. Every trace-SQL GPU query selects category GLOB 'gpu*', so macOS window-host GPU time was invisible to them rather than merely mislabelled: nothing failed, the frame rendered, and the flushed trace looked complete. The fix changes only the category argument of those three PULP_TRACE_SCOPE_NAMED calls in core/view/platform/mac/window_host_mac.mm; no span names, no timing, no renderer, backend, font, asset or Skia pin moves, and no fixture, snapshot or threshold changes. The gate is a source-level invariant (trace-span-category-lint) rather than a runtime assertion, because driving the mac window host needs a window server and a runtime check self-skips on every headless runner, and a skip is not a pass. render-assets-and-backends is crossed by that single .mm file. Registered as watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a change that crossed its selector. No authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes.
